chapters.draft: Owns the appointment booking functionality enabling patients to book appointments at any time through the online service. Does not own clinical records or prescriptions. Also excludes handling phone booking registration, appointment changes or cancellations by receptionist, appointment reminders by text or email, and responses to those reminders.

chapters.record: TC-001 Compute for Appointment scheduling service
chapters.draft: Provide the compute capability required by APP-001 Appointment scheduling service to run its owned application logic, enabling patients to book appointments online at any time.

chapters.record: TR-001 Compute for Appointment scheduling service implementation
chapters.draft: Operations ownership and support are currently unassigned; the plan for monitoring, incident handling, and operational responsibilities is open and requires definition. Given the compute serves the Appointment scheduling service, defining telemetry, automated failure detection, and incident response processes consistent with microservices operational obligations is necessary. Further clarity on ownership, monitoring tools, and escalation protocols is needed before implementation.

The failure policy is currently undefined; the design notes this as an open question regarding the caller's behavior when the outcome is unavailable or uncertain. No specific error handling or rejection semantics are stated in the brief or upstream requirements, indicating that this must be clarified by the architect or stakeholders before implementation.

The control mechanism for limiting access to Appointment is currently unspecified and remains an open question in the design. No details are provided in the brief or upstream records on where and how access control is enforced. The control addresses the threat of unauthorized disclosure when callers without a need to know access appointment data, aiming to protect confidential journey information. Consideration is indicated towards ensuring there is a security-relevant responsibility or capability within the scope to enforce policy decisions, potentially requiring defined ownership, monitoring, and failure handling aligned with anti-single-point-of-failure guidance. Verification involves attempting the known threat scenario to assess enforcement and audit trail capture once the mechanism is implemented.

chapters.record: SDD Sol live check · reference — Solution Design
chapters.draft: This design enables patients to book, move, or cancel outpatient appointments anytime, ensuring all freed slots are offered to a waiting list prior to the appointment day. It focuses on outpatient scheduling from booking through follow-up, excluding clinical records and prescriptions, while considering data privacy, reminder content constraints, performance versus transaction integrity trade-offs, and compliance with the requirement for live online booking by year-end.
